controls.title: Technical security verification
gaps: Commissioned independent penetration test and remediation report are not complete.

controls.title: Release integrity, SBOM, signing, and provenance
Identity, authorization, and tenant isolation
gaps: A supported reference host profile now renders network identity, authenticated TLS, process and filesystem isolation, resource ceilings, default-deny networking, and one-tenant-per-process-and-store routing, gated by scripts/verify_host_profile.py. The deploying organization must still substitute its own trust domain, client identities, artifact digests, and secret material, and no such deployment has been independently assessed.

loomd now opens its store with Loom::open_production_attested under the reference profile, so writes over the MCP surface are signature-authenticated against a governance-signed actor registry and a declared rollback floor, and a registry that cannot be verified stops startup. What remains deployment-owned is the key material itself: issuing and custodying the actor-governance signing key, distributing and rotating each actor's key, and revoking a compromised one by raising the attested generation. No customer key ceremony or revocation drill has been evidenced.

controls.title: Key management and cryptographic trust
gaps: Production HSM/KMS key custody, delivery, revocation, and rotation drill are deployment-owned and not yet evidenced.

controls.title: Data protection, privacy, and retention
gaps: Encryption at rest/in transit, retention, deletion, residency, and privacy notices are host or managed-service responsibilities.

controls.title: Backup, recovery, and resilience
gaps: The reference profile now renders scheduled signed backups against a platform-provided point-in-time clone, an independent verification job that runs under a different identity and holds only the public trust root, retention with legal hold, a declared immutable off-account target with a named WORM mechanism, and a restore rehearsal that restores to a fresh path and cannot overwrite or activate a live store. The engine holds an exclusive lock on its store, so no job can read a live tenant volume; the profile refuses to render one that tries.

Customer-scale RPO/RTO targets and a signed restore drill receipt for each target topology remain required. maxAgeSeconds is a threshold the profile enforces, not a recovery objective anyone has measured, and no drill has been executed against a production storage stack, CSI driver, or backup product.

controls.title: Operational observability and bounded admission
gaps: Backup, verification, retention, and scrub signals are emitted as fixed-cardinality unlabelled series and are wired to rendered alerts for a stale backup, an unverified backup, a failing job, and detected damage; the stale rule fires on absence so a job that never ran is not read as health. No signal carries a tenant identifier. What remains deployment-owned is the collection pipeline itself: no metric here has been scraped by a production collector, no alert has been routed to a named on-call rota, and no threshold has been tuned against observed behaviour.

controls.title: Incident and vulnerability response
gaps: Named on-call staff, communication channels, and an exercised customer notification drill are organizational gates.

externalGates.title: Independent penetration test
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Signed final report; all critical/high findings remediated or risk-accepted by the CISO.

externalGates.title: Production-topology recovery exercise
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Signed drill receipt proves approved RPO/RTO on customer-scale data using the target storage and backup stack.

externalGates.title: HSM/KMS trust-root ceremony and rotation
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Dual-control key ceremony, non-exportable production keys, revocation path, and completed rotation drill.

externalGates.title: Support, incident, SLA, and escalation readiness
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Named 24x7 escalation rota, contracted support targets, status communications, and exercised incident notification procedure.

externalGates.title: Organizational assurance and contractual package
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Buyer-required SIG/CAIQ, DPA, subprocessor/residency disclosure, and applicable SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence approved.
